key_insight: This paper is the first to establish scaling laws for uniform-state and interpolating discrete diffusion language models, showing they scale differently than Masked diffusion. It also demonstrates that Masked diffusion can be made ≈12% more FLOPs-efficient with a simple training modification.
problem_solved: Clarifies how different discrete diffusion formulations scale with model size and compute, and reduces computational cost of Masked diffusion to make diffusion-based generation more practical compared to autoregressive approaches.
method: Empirical scaling-law study across model sizes and compute budgets for uniform-state and interpolating discrete diffusion methods.
Direct comparison to Masked diffusion on language modeling benchmarks (e.g., perplexity and compute cost).
Introduce and evaluate a straightforward training modification that yields ~12% FLOPs savings for Masked diffusion models.
impact: Provides guidance for researchers and engineers choosing between diffusion formulations as they scale, and offers an easy optimization to reduce training/inference FLOPs—helpful for lowering cost and improving throughput of diffusion LMs.
visual_elements: Scaling-law plot: loss/perplexity vs. compute/model size for Masked, uniform-state, and interpolating diffusion (log–log axes).
Bar chart showing FLOPs and relative % improvement (≈12%) before and after the proposed training change for Masked diffusion.
Schematic diagram comparing the three discrete diffusion workflows (Masked, uniform-state, interpolating) with example token transitions.
Latency/throughput icon panel: chips/stopwatch icons summarizing generation speed and compute cost trade-offs.
paper_title: Scaling Beyond Masked Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Jean-Marie Lemercier, Zhihan Yang, Justin Deschenaux, Jingyu Liu
